subject: Delegated runbook & fallback procedures request - Lucent Labs
messages:
From: Avery Cole <avery.cole@lucentlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@lucentlabs.com
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delegated runbook and fallback procedures - next steps

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward a Private deployment of Redwood in our VPC, security and ops want a clear, signed-runbook that spells out which operational responsibilities Lucent Labs retains vs. Redwood.

Specifically we need:
- A runbook outlining normal failover/fallback steps (including who performs which actions).
- Clarification of latency uptime SLOs and any exclusions for customer-controlled network (peering, NAT gateways, KMS).
- The evidence we can expect (audit logs, monitoring endpoints) to validate uptime/latency attribution.

Can Redwood share a runbook template and a proposed addendum we can review with procurement and our security team? Also flag any items that will require exceptions to the standard SLA.

Attached: lucent_network_topology.pdf (high level network diagram).

Best,
Avery
Avery Cole
Head of Cloud Ops, Lucent Labs
avery.cole@lucentlabs.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegated runbook and fallback procedures - next steps

Hi Avery —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can definitely provide a runbook template plus a draft addendum that enumerates shared responsibilities and the recommended carveouts for customer-controlled infra. Quick notes:
- We typically exclude customer-managed network faults (peering/transit) and KMS latency from our uptime SLA unless we operate the component.
- We provide tracing and token-level latency metrics via the Console; for Private deployments we can enable an audit export stream (can discuss retention).

I'll loop in Karthik (platform/ops) and Vanessa (legal engagement) to put a draft on Drive and call out items that need sign-off. Would you be available for a 30-minute review on Wednesday 21 May at 09:00 PT?

If that works I'll share the draft addendum and a runbook stub in advance.

Thanks,
Soji n

Subject: Re: Delegated runbook and fallback procedures - draft addendum

On Mon, May 19, 2025 at 10:02 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll loop in Karthik (platform/ops) and Vanessa (legal engagement) to put a draft on Drive and call out items that need sign-off.

Hi team —

Attached is a working draft: draft-delegation-addendum.docx (internal). High-level summary of what we recommend include in the addendum:

1) Operational ownership matrix (who performs: peering diagnostics, route-table changes, NAT gateway failover, on-prem firewall changes).
2) Attribution rules for latency and downtime (examples + measurement points):
   - If backend token generation latency > configured SLO but network hop time between customer edge and Redwood infra accounts for >50% of tail, issue credited SLA exception.
   - KMS operations initiated in-customer (customer-managed KMS) are excluded from Redwood availability for key-encryption dependent requests.
3) Evidence & monitoring:
   - Redwood will provide per-request traces, per-route latency histograms, and an audit log export (S3 or SFTP).
   - Recommended retention: 90 days (can negotiate longer under Enterprise).
4) Fallback/playbook:
   - Prefix-caching and graceful model downgrade steps we can execute; we'll also document the ops steps for the customer to fail traffic to a hot-standby region if needed.

Open items for Lucent Labs:
- Do you want Redwood to operate a managed NAT/egress (we can, for a fee) or do you prefer to retain that under your control?
- Who is the designated network on-call for Lucent (name + escalation phone)?

Link to draft folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cRunbookDraft

I'll be on the call Wednesday and can walk the operational examples.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Avery Cole <avery.cole@lucentlabs.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@lucentlabs.com
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegated runbook and fallback procedures - Lucent review

Soojin / Karthik —

Thanks for the draft and the call earlier today. A few follow-ups from security and procurement:

- Security asks for a short playbook demonstrating how Redwood would detect a customer-edge packet loss event and what telemetry we receive to attribute latency to our infra vs. Lucent's network.
- Procurement needs explicit language for the SLA exclusion clause and an example incident timeline showing when an exception would be applied and the customer notification cadence.
- Attached is a Lucent network diagram to highlight peered segments we control (lucent_network_topology.pdf).

Can Redwood provide the playbook (1–2 pages) and the incident timeline example so we can attach to the procurement addendum? If Redwood can also provide a signed copy of the addendum for DocuSign, that would speed approvals.

Best,
Avery

Subject: Re: Delegated runbook and fallback procedures - finalized next steps

Avery —

Appreciate the clear asks; attached are the items we discussed: runbook_v1.pdf (2-page playbook with detection & immediate ops actions) and network-diagram.png (annotated with responsibility ownership). The draft addendum has been updated and placed in the Drive folder; we've also added an incident timeline example inside the doc.

High-level summary of the agreement we will ask Lucent for signature on:
- Redwood SLOs remain as published, except for exclusions where Latency/Availability is caused by customer-controlled network or customer-managed KMS.
- Exceptions are assessed using the attribution rules in section 2 of the addendum; Redwood will produce the requested traces and histograms within 48 hours of an incident to support attribution.
- For customers that opt-in for Redwood-managed egress/NAT, certain exclusions are removed in exchange for managed egress fees (pricing TBD).

Next steps:
1) Please review runbook_v1.pdf and the revised addendum in the Drive folder.
2) If accepted, reply with a confirmation email addressed to procure@lucentlabs.com and we will push the addendum to DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/XYZ-1234

Attachments: runbook_v1.pdf, network-diagram.png

I'll also attach a redline-ready DOCX (signed-addendum.docx) to the folder for legal. Let me know if you want Redwood to operate egress for a pilot.

Thanks,
So oj in
